hook_text: Why is World TB Day held on the twenty-fourth of March? Because on that day in 1882, a German doctor announced something extraordinary.
clip_script: Berlin, the twenty-fourth of March 1882. Robert Koch tells a room of scientists that he has found the tiny rod-shaped germ that causes tuberculosis, one of the deadliest diseases in the world. He used dyes to stain germs, grew them on jelly and photographed them through a microscope. Today, TB can be cured with medicine, but only if patients take every dose for six months. South Africa still fights TB every day.
visual_style: Whiteboard microscope view of rod-shaped germs stained purple, a Petri dish with spots of bacteria, then a South African clinic with a nurse handing out medicine and an open window.
mood: Serious but hopeful, like a detective solving a case that still matters today.
pacing: A dramatic announcement, then step-by-step methods, then a practical guide to TB today.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and make a poster with three signs of TB and three ways to prevent it.
